# Central Networks Coupled with Multi-Domain Environmental Heatmaps

`cliomicplot` provides a composable Grammar of Graphics layer system to couple central modular co-occurrence networks with peripheral multi-domain correlation heatmaps.

## Architecture and Coordinate System

The layout operates on a unified Cartesian coordinate system centered at $(0, 0)$ spanning $[-7.4, 7.4]$ on both axes:

1. **Central Network Ring ($r \le 2.80$)**: Contains modular network nodes, intra-module edge connections, cluster hulls, and radial module badges.
2. **Annular Link Corridor ($2.80 < r < 4.0$)**: Separates the central network perimeter from the peripheral heatmaps. Outer boundary dots mark $r \approx 3.38$.
3. **Corner Triangular Heatmaps**: Four triangular correlation heatmaps occupy the corners. Diagonal indicator points connect via curved segments to central modules.
4. **Inter-Domain Links**: Curved lines originate from peripheral indicators and connect to central module perimeters. Line width scales with statistical significance ($-\log_{10}P$), and color denotes correlation direction.

## Layered Grammar of Graphics

The grammar separates coordinate computation from geometry rendering:

- `cli_env_network_data()`: Computes spatial layouts, node positions, intra-module edges, cluster convex hulls, triangular heatmap coordinates, and link trajectories. Returns an S3 object of class `cli_env_network_data`.
- `geom_env_boundary()`: Draws the circular boundary ring at $r = 2.80$ and the outer concentric dots at $r \approx 3.38$.
- `geom_env_central_network()`: Draws central intra-module edges, cluster convex hulls, node glyphs (shape 16 fill-only), and module label badges.
- `geom_env_corner_heatmaps()`: Draws triangular correlation tiles, significance asterisks or correlation values, diagonal connector points, 78° angled variable labels, and domain titles.
- `geom_env_links()`: Draws curved inter-domain connecting lines weighted by significance and direction.
- `coord_env_network()`: Enforces a 1:1 circular aspect ratio with standard viewport boundaries (`xlim = c(-7.4, 7.4), ylim = c(-7.4, 7.4)`).
- `theme_env_network()`: Removes Cartesian grid lines and axis ticks while positioning a multi-tier publication legend.

### Composing with the `+` Operator


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(cliomicplot)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Generate grammatical data object
d <- cli_env_network_data(preset = "nature", show_values = TRUE)

# 2. Assemble plot layer by layer
p_grammar <- ggplot() +
  geom_env_boundary(data = d) +
  geom_env_central_network(data = d) +
  geom_env_corner_heatmaps(data = d) +
  geom_env_links(data = d) +
  coord_env_network() +
  theme_env_network(preset = "nature") +
  labs(title = "Layer-by-Layer Grammar Assembly (Nature Preset)")

p_grammar
```

![](13-coupled-environmental-networks_files/figure-html/grammar-demo-1.png){width=2550}

## Formula Interface

You can call `cliplot()` using formula syntax `env_data ~ comm_data`:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(42)
# Community abundance matrix: 20 samples, 7 taxa
comm <- matrix(rpois(140, lambda = 12), nrow = 20, ncol = 7,
               dimnames = list(paste0("S", 1:20), paste0("Taxon_", 1:7)))

# Environmental correlation matrices for 4 domains
make_cor <- function(vars) {
  p <- length(vars)
  m <- matrix(runif(p * p, 0.2, 0.8), p, p)
  diag(m) <- 1.0
  m[lower.tri(m)] <- t(m)[lower.tri(m)]
  dimnames(m) <- list(vars, vars)
  m
}

env_domains <- list(
  "Biophysical" = make_cor(c("pH", "Moisture", "Organic_C")),
  "Nutrients"   = make_cor(c("Nitrogen", "Phosphorus", "Potassium")),
  "Trace_Metals"= make_cor(c("Zinc", "Copper", "Iron")),
  "Climate"     = make_cor(c("Temp", "Rainfall", "Humidity"))
)

# One-line formula dispatch
p_formula <- cliplot(
  env_domains ~ comm,
  type   = "env_network",
  preset = "clinical",
  title  = "Formula Dispatch: env_domains ~ comm_abundance"
)
p_formula
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](13-coupled-environmental-networks_files/figure-html/formula-demo-1.png){width=2550}
:::
:::


## The 7 Publisher Style Presets

The package provides 7 styling presets for different journal and biological contexts:

| Preset | Central Network | Peripheral Domains | Palette Aesthetics |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `clinical` / `nature`| Multi-module microbiome | Biophysical, Severity, Cytokines, Exposome | Nature Slate Blue, Crimson, Amber |
| `seasonal` | Seasonal succession | Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter | Flora Green, Solar Amber, Rust, Frost Blue |
| `dark` | Luminescent multi-omics| 4 Multi-omics layers | Obsidian background, neon cyan & magenta |
| `lancet` | Clinical epidemiology | Clinical trials exposome | Muted greys, thin editorial strokes |
| `multi_tissue` | Multi-tissue axis | Epidermis, Dermis, Serum, Gut | Terracotta, Cerulean, Amethyst, Forest |
| `circadian` | Diurnal oscillations | Dawn (06:00), Midday (12:00), Dusk (18:00), Midnight (24:00) | Dawn Rose, Noon Gold, Dusk Indigo, Midnight Navy |
| `bipolar` | Differential coupling | Healthy vs Disease contrasts | Polar divergent Crimson vs Deep Blue |

## Triangular Correlation Heatmap with Curved Mantel Links: `type = "mantel_triangle"`

While the 4-corner canvas of `cliplot_env_network()` accommodates up to four independent environmental domains simultaneously, ecological microbiome studies frequently link pairwise environmental variables with target taxonomic phyla using lower-triangular correlation heatmaps and curved Mantel test arcs (`MatCorPlot2` in `ggClusterNet 2`, Wen et al. *iMeta* 2025; `linkET`).

`type_mantel_triangle()` pairs in-tile correlation values ($r$) and significance asterisks with smooth bezier arcs scaled by Mantel correlation magnitude and colored by $p$-value tiers:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p_mantel <- cliplot(
  type  = type_mantel_triangle(label_size = 2.8, node_size = 3.8),
  title = "Environmental Factors Coupled with Microbial Phyla (Mantel Correlation)"
)
p_mantel
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](13-coupled-environmental-networks_files/figure-html/mantel-triangle-book-1.png){width=2400}
